reply.text:
I can't put a number on caffeine for you, and that goes for energy drinks too. Three before a session is enough that I'd run it past a doctor or a dietitian, who can speak to your situation, including any medications or health conditions.

In general terms, energy drinks stack caffeine on top of whatever else you have in a day, and the amount varies a lot from brand to brand. It's worth reading the labels on the cans you drink.

On the training side, your sleep, a proper meal an hour or two before, and water do most of the work a drink is being asked to do. If energy before the gym is a regular struggle, tell me how your week looks and we can see whether the schedule or the session setup is the problem.
